questions.stem: Why is depreciation important in accounting?

options.text: It increases the value of assets.
It matches the cost of an asset with its revenue.
It is used to inflate profits.

questions.explanation: Depreciation is crucial for matching the cost of an asset with the revenue it generates, adhering to the matching principle in accounting.

distractorRationale.a: Depreciation decreases the value of assets, not increases.
distractorRationale.b: Depreciation is legal and used for accounting purposes, not tax evasion.
distractorRationale.d: Depreciation reduces profits by allocating asset costs over time.

questions.stem: How is depreciation recorded in the ledger?

options.text: As a credit to the asset account and a debit to the depreciation expense account.
As a debit to the asset account and a credit to the depreciation expense account.
As a debit to the cash account and a credit to the asset account.
As a credit to the cash account and a debit to the asset account.

questions.explanation: Depreciation is recorded by crediting the asset account to reduce its value and debiting the depreciation expense account to reflect the cost.

distractorRationale.b: The asset account is credited, not debited, to reduce its value.
distractorRationale.c: Cash is not involved in depreciation entries.
distractorRationale.d: Cash is not involved in depreciation entries.

questions.stem: A vehicle costing ₦800,000 is depreciated using the reducing-balance method at 25% per annum. What is the depreciation for the first year?
questions.explanation: The reducing-balance method calculates depreciation as a percentage of the book value. 25% of ₦800,000 is ₦200,000.

distractorRationale.a: This is the straight-line method result, not reducing-balance.
distractorRationale.b: This is an incorrect percentage calculation.
distractorRationale.c: This is an incorrect percentage calculation.

questions.stem: Which method of depreciation is more suitable for assets that lose value quickly?
questions.explanation: The reducing-balance method is suitable for assets that lose value quickly as it allocates more depreciation in the earlier years.

distractorRationale.a: Straight-line method allocates equal depreciation each year.
distractorRationale.c: Sum-of-the-years-digits is another accelerated method but not as common.
distractorRationale.d: Units of production is based on usage, not time.
